title: Kenyan Coconut Milkshake
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Kenyan Coconut Milkshake — thick coconut cream blended with vanilla ice cream, toasted coconut, and a touch of cardamom. Rich, fragrant, and tropical — the Swahili coast in a glass.
longDesc: The Kenyan coconut milkshake draws on the coastal love of coconut to create the richest, most fragrant milkshake in the café repertoire. The toasted coconut garnish and cardamom are the coastal signatures.
ingredients: Whipped cream and toasted coconut — for topping
steps: Toast desiccated coconut in a dry pan until golden. Cool.
Blend coconut cream, ice cream, honey, cardamom, vanilla, and ice until smooth.
Top with whipped cream and toasted coconut.
chefTips: Thick coconut cream gives a richer result than coconut milk.
The cardamom is the coastal Kenyan signature — do not skip it.
Toast the coconut fresh for maximum crunch.
commonMistakes: Using thin coconut milk — insufficient richness.
cookingScience: Coconut cream has a higher fat content (20—25%) than coconut milk (10—15%). The higher fat content creates a richer, more stable emulsion when blended with ice cream — producing a thicker shake with more body.
sustainabilityTips: Use coconut cream from sustainably grown coastal Kenyan coconuts.
healthBenefits: Best enjoyed as an occasional treat.
culturalNote: The coconut milkshake brings the Swahili coast's love of coconut into the modern café context — a drink that tastes of the sea breeze and the palm trees even in a Nairobi high street café.
